source.market_name: Will the Iranian regime fall before 2027?

market_name: Will the Iranian regime fall before 2027?

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether the probability move coincides with a concrete headline (strike, coup, mass unrest) or is idiosyncratic; check Brent/WTI futures and Hormuz tanker news for corroboration.
time_plan.1h: Compare USO/crude futures move against the probability shift magnitude; verify the front-month backwardation and options skew (call demand) are rising.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether the oil move is holding or fading; watch for OPEC/US strategic-reserve commentary that could cap the spike.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate if the escalation narrative is confirmed by multiple credible outlets or being walked back; adjust conviction accordingly.
time_plan.12h: Mark final crude move vs. prediction; note whether risk premium persisted or reversed as the news was digested.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of the Iranian regime falling would almost certainly coincide with a discrete escalation event — large-scale conflict, external strikes, civil war, or an oil-infrastructure/Strait of Hormuz disruption. Iran produces ~3mbd and sits astride ~20% of seaborne oil transit, so any credible instability scenario carries a large supply-risk premium. In the short 12h window the market prices the disruption/conflict risk, which pushes crude up sharply, regardless of whether an eventual regime change is bullish or bearish for oil over the long run.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether gold spot and GLD are ticking up alongside a risk-off move in equities and a bid in USD/CHF/JPY.
time_plan.1h: Confirm the safe-haven bid is broad (bonds, gold, USD) rather than isolated; distinguish genuine flight-to-safety from noise.
time_plan.2h: Watch real yields and DXY — a strong dollar could blunt gold's gain; reassess magnitude.
time_plan.6h: Determine if geopolitical premium is sustaining across sessions or mean-reverting.
time_plan.12h: Record final gold move and whether the safe-haven thesis held; note if it stayed sub-threshold as expected.

predictions.reasoning: A jump in regime-collapse probability signals acute Middle East geopolitical stress, which typically drives safe-haven demand into gold. Gold reacts to conflict/uncertainty in the short window even before macro fundamentals shift. Magnitude is smaller than oil because gold is a diffuse hedge rather than directly supply-exposed; likely below the 700bps tradable threshold.

evidence_used: Iran is a major oil producer (~3mbd) and controls the Strait of Hormuz, through which ~20% of global oil flows
Regime-collapse scenarios (revolution, civil war, coup, external strikes) are strongly correlated with regional conflict and oil-supply disruption
Historical pattern: Middle East escalation events produce oil spikes and safe-haven gold/USD bids in intraday windows
Prediction market probability shifts on military_conflict topics often precede or coincide with escalation headlines
uncertainty_notes: A probability move may reflect slow-burn political speculation, not an imminent disruption — in which case oil barely moves
Regime change could paradoxically be read as de-escalatory/oil-bearish if it implies removal of a conflict actor and eventual sanctions relief
The market question spans through end-2026, so a 12h probability twitch may carry little near-term asset signal
Proxy risk: USO has roll/contango drag vs. spot crude; GLD is only a partial geopolitical hedge
This scenario may already be partially priced if a headline is public before the anomaly is observed

llm_justification.summary: A sharp upward move in the implied probability that the Iranian regime falls would most plausibly coincide with acute Middle East escalation, which pushes crude oil higher via a supply-risk premium (Hormuz/Iranian output exposure) and provides a smaller safe-haven bid to gold. Oil is the cleaner, higher-magnitude proxy and can plausibly clear the 700bps tradable threshold on a genuine escalation; gold is a secondary, weaker hedge likely below threshold. Confidence is modest because the direction of the underlying event (conflict-driven spike vs. eventual de-escalation) and whether the signal is news-driven are both uncertain.
key_assumptions: A probability spike is driven by, or anticipates, a concrete escalation/conflict event rather than idle speculation
Markets price the near-term supply-disruption risk more heavily than long-run regime-change outcomes in a 12h window
Oil and gold remain liquid and responsive to Middle East geopolitical headlines
failure_modes: The move reverses within hours as the news is denied or fades, dragging crude back down
The escalation is interpreted as de-escalatory (regime removed = less conflict, sanctions relief), making oil bearish — direction flips
The information was already public and fully priced before the market anomaly appeared
The probability shift is idiosyncratic/low-liquidity noise on the prediction market with no real-world catalyst
USO/GLD are weak proxies for the specific supply channel; the actual move concentrates in Brent spreads or regional equities not captured here
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
